questions.question: Flexion and extension movements occur in which plane and about which axis?

options.A: Sagittal plane about a vertical axis
options.B: Sagittal plane about a frontal (mediolateral) axis
options.C: Transverse plane about a vertical axis
options.D: Frontal plane about a sagittal axis

questions.explanation: Abduction/adduction occur in the frontal plane about an anteroposterior axis; rotation occurs in the transverse plane about a vertical axis.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Abduction and adduction of the hip occur in the:
questions.explanation: Axis: anteroposterior (sagittal).
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Medial and lateral rotation of the humerus occur in the:

options.A: Transverse (horizontal) plane about a vertical axis
options.B: Coronal plane about a transverse axis

questions.explanation: Pronation/supination and spinal rotation are also transverse plane movements.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Osteokinematics describes:

options.C: The movement of bones in space (e.g. flexion, abduction)
options.D: The movement of joint surfaces relative to each other

questions.explanation: Arthrokinematics describes roll, slide (glide) and spin of joint surfaces.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The three arthrokinematic movements of joint surfaces are:
questions.explanation: In most joints a combination of roll and slide occurs.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The instantaneous centre of rotation of a joint is:

options.A: The point where force is applied
options.C: The point about which one segment is rotating relative to the other at a given instant
options.D: The centre of gravity of the segment

questions.explanation: At the knee the centre of rotation migrates during flexion because of the shape of the femoral condyles.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which movement occurs in the frontal plane?
questions.explanation: Elbow and knee flexion occur in the sagittal plane.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The shoulder (glenohumeral) joint has how many degrees of freedom?
questions.explanation: A ball-and-socket joint allows flexion/extension, abduction/adduction and rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The metacarpophalangeal joint is a:

options.D: Condyloid (ellipsoid) joint with two degrees of freedom

questions.explanation: Allows flexion/extension and abduction/adduction but little axial rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The interphalangeal joints of the fingers are:
questions.explanation: Uniaxial: flexion and extension only.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The force couple that produces upward rotation of the scapula during arm elevation involves:

options.D: Upper and lower trapezius with serratus anterior

questions.explanation: Together they rotate the glenoid upward so the humerus can elevate.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The scapular plane (scaption) lies at about:
questions.explanation: Elevation in the scapular plane places the supraspinatus at an optimal length and the capsule untwisted.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The subacromial space is narrowest at about:
questions.explanation: Hence the impingement ‘painful arc’.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The elbow flexion arc required for most activities of daily living is approximately:
questions.explanation: Morrey: 30–130° flexion, with 50° pronation and 50° supination.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The axis of wrist flexion/extension passes through the:
questions.explanation: The capitate head is the centre of rotation for both flexion/extension and radial/ulnar deviation.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: In a power grip the wrist is typically positioned in:
questions.explanation: Wrist extensors lengthen the finger flexors at an optimal length.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Picking up a pin between the thumb and index finger is an example of a:
questions.explanation: Tip-to-tip pinch uses FPL and FDP; pulp pinch uses interossei and FPB.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The lumbricals act to produce:
questions.explanation: Together with the interossei they are the ‘intrinsic-plus’ muscles.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The dorsal interossei of the hand:

options.B: Abduct the fingers from the middle finger (DAB)

questions.explanation: Palmar interossei adduct toward the middle finger (PAD); ulnar nerve.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: During single-leg stance the hip joint reaction force is approximately:

options.B: Three to four times body weight

questions.explanation: Abductor muscle force needed to balance the pelvis is about 2½ times body weight, adding to the joint load.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Using a cane in the contralateral hand reduces the hip joint reaction force on the affected hip because it:

options.D: Decreases the abductor muscle force required to balance the pelvis

questions.explanation: A cane held opposite provides a counter-moment with a long lever arm.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: In coxa vara the abductor muscle lever arm is:

options.C: Increased, reducing the force needed for balance

questions.explanation: Coxa valga decreases the lever arm and increases the joint load.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which muscle is the main lateral rotator of the hip in extension?
questions.explanation: The deep six lateral rotators include piriformis, obturators, gemelli and quadratus femoris.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The patellofemoral joint reaction force is greatest in:
questions.explanation: PFJ force increases with knee flexion due to the quadriceps tension and the angle of the patellar tendon.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which factor increases the Q-angle?

options.A: Femoral anteversion, genu valgum or lateral tibial torsion

questions.explanation: A larger Q-angle increases the lateral pull on the patella.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The anteromedial bundle of the ACL is tightest in:
questions.explanation: The posterolateral bundle is tight in extension.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The posterior cruciate ligament resists:

options.C: Posterior translation of the tibia on the femur

questions.explanation: It is the primary restraint to posterior tibial translation.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The medial collateral ligament primarily resists:
questions.explanation: The LCL resists varus stress.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The windlass mechanism of the foot refers to:

options.B: Tightening of the plantar fascia on great toe extension that raises the medial longitudinal arch
options.C: Lowering of the arch during dorsiflexion

questions.explanation: Occurs in late stance during push-off.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: During the loading response, subtalar pronation functions to:

options.B: Unlock the midfoot and absorb shock
options.D: Lock the foot as a rigid lever

questions.explanation: Supination during late stance locks the foot for push-off.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: In push-off during gait, the major force is generated by the:
questions.explanation: The calf muscles provide about 80% of propulsion.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Genu recurvatum (knee hyperextension in stance) can result from weakness of the:

options.C: Quadriceps or from a plantar flexion contracture

questions.explanation: The knee is forced backward to maintain stability.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The greatest range of cervical flexion/extension occurs at:
questions.explanation: C1–C2 provides most rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Lumbar spine rotation is limited mainly by:

options.C: The orientation of the facet joints (sagittal)

questions.explanation: Only about 5° occurs in the whole lumbar spine.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The nucleus pulposus of an intervertebral disc is composed mainly of:
questions.explanation: The annulus fibrosus has concentric lamellae of collagen.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Disc height is greatest:

options.B: In the morning after nocturnal rehydration

questions.explanation: Height changes by about 1–2 cm during the day.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The ligamentum flavum connects the:
questions.explanation: It is rich in elastin and helps restore the upright posture.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Thoracic spine rotation is greater than lumbar rotation because:

options.B: The facets lie in the coronal plane

questions.explanation: Thoracic movements are limited by the rib cage in flexion and extension.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The ‘pump-handle’ movement of the upper ribs during inspiration increases the:
questions.explanation: The ‘bucket-handle’ movement of lower ribs increases the transverse dimension.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The main accessory muscles of inspiration include the:
questions.explanation: Forced expiration uses abdominal muscles and internal intercostals.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Intra-abdominal pressure during lifting helps to:

options.A: Unload the lumbar spine by acting as a pressurised column

questions.explanation: Contraction of transversus abdominis and the diaphragm raises pressure.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The spinal load is least when a weight is lifted:

options.C: Close to the body with a neutral spine

questions.explanation: Longer moment arm increases compressive force.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Increasing the base of support makes a person:
questions.explanation: A cane or walker widens the base.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: In quiet standing the body sways about the:
questions.explanation: Ankle strategy controls small perturbations.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: In the standing position the line of gravity passes:

options.A: Through the centre of the ankle
options.D: Anterior to the ankle and knee axes and posterior to the hip axis

questions.explanation: Hence the ankle plantar flexors work to prevent forward sway.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: In a swayback posture the typical muscle findings are:

options.A: Tight hip flexors and hamstrings with weak external oblique and upper back extensors

questions.explanation: Hips shift forward and the trunk extends backward.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Forward head posture places increased load on the:

options.B: Cervical extensors and posterior cervical structures

questions.explanation: Each additional inch of forward head increases the head's effective weight.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Compared with walking, in running:

options.A: There is a flight phase with no double support

questions.explanation: The stance phase decreases to about 40% of the cycle.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The normal step width (walking base) is approximately:
questions.explanation: A wide-based gait suggests cerebellar ataxia or balance problems.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Double support in normal walking occupies about:
questions.explanation: It is reduced when walking speed increases.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The normal vertical displacement of the centre of gravity during walking is about:
questions.explanation: Lateral displacement is also about 5 cm; determinants of gait reduce the energy cost.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Which muscle acts eccentrically at initial contact to control foot lowering?
questions.explanation: Weakness produces foot slap.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Initial swing is characterised by:

options.D: Hip and knee flexion with ankle dorsiflexion to clear the foot

questions.explanation: Iliopsoas and hamstrings act; the foot clears the ground at mid-swing.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Walking up stairs requires a greater range of which joint motion than level walking?
questions.explanation: Hip flexion about 60° and knee flexion about 90° are needed.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Compared with young adults, elderly walkers typically show:

options.D: Reduced step length, speed and push-off with increased double support

questions.explanation: Decline in ankle power is notable.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: As the pennation angle of a muscle increases:

options.D: The muscle can pack more fibres, increasing force capacity but reducing the effective pull along the tendon

questions.explanation: Pennate muscles favour force production over range.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Co-contraction of agonist and antagonist muscles around a joint primarily increases:
questions.explanation: Used in closed-chain exercises and in joint instability.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The stretch–shortening cycle improves performance mainly through:

options.B: Storage and release of elastic energy and the stretch reflex

questions.explanation: Used in jumping and running.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Compared with muscle, tendons are:

options.C: Stiffer and able to withstand greater tensile force with little extension

questions.explanation: Tendons store elastic energy and transmit force.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Ligaments typically fail when strained beyond approximately:
questions.explanation: Strains above 4% cause microfailure.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Bone is strongest against:

options.B: Compression, then tension, and weakest against shear

questions.explanation: Hence oblique and spiral fractures occur with shear/torsion.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Articular cartilage resists compression mainly because of:

options.C: Its high proteoglycan content and water retention

questions.explanation: Collagen resists tension and shear.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: Prolonged immobilisation of a joint leads to:

options.B: Cartilage degeneration, capsular contracture and muscle atrophy

questions.explanation: Remobilisation should be gradual.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The torque that a muscle can produce varies with joint angle. This relationship is called the:
questions.explanation: Resisted exercise machines use cams to match the torque curve.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: The moment arm of a muscle at a joint is the:

options.D: Perpendicular distance from the joint axis to the line of action of the muscle force

questions.explanation: Maximum torque is generated when the muscle acts at 90° to the bone.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)

questions.question: At an angle of pull of 90° a muscle's force is entirely:
questions.explanation: At small angles most of the force is stabilising (compressive) or distracting.
questions.sourceBook: Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
